acceptedAnswer.text: LandCheck Estates is a web workspace for Nigerian property developers to plan estate layouts, digitize and manage plots, handle buyer reservations and payments, screen sites for flood/erosion/soil risk, and market the estate - all from one dashboard.

mainEntity.name: Can I import an existing estate layout into LandCheck Estates?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. You can bring in a layout from a CSV file, GIS/GeoJSON data, a CAD (DXF) drawing, or even a scanned paper plan, then georeference and digitize the plots, roads, drainage, and open space.

mainEntity.name: Does LandCheck Estates support WhatsApp and social media marketing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. It includes a built-in WhatsApp inbox to message buyers and leads, automatic Facebook and Instagram post scheduling with in-dashboard comment replies and likes, SMS/email customer notifications, and QR-coded marketing campaigns to track leads by channel.

mainEntity.name: Does LandCheck Estates screen for flood risk and soil conditions?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Every estate and plot can be screened for flood and erosion risk, plus an indicative soil analysis covering a presumptive bearing-capacity range, a water-table tendency, and a 0-2m soil texture profile - with a one-click option to request a licensed geotechnical survey for any foundation decision.

mainEntity.name: How does LandCheck Estates help prevent land scams?

acceptedAnswer.text: A buyer can check any plot number or agent code against the developer's own public Estate page before paying anyone, staff can mark a plot's title as verified once they've reviewed the documents, and every estate can show live progress on its government approvals - Survey Plan, Layout, Governor's Consent, and Certificate of Occupancy - so nothing is taken on trust.

mainEntity.name: Can intending buyers verify a plot's GPS location remotely?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. On the Enterprise plan, a site agent opens a live video call with a remote buyer and shares their GPS position in real time, verified against the plot's actual boundary, so diaspora and out-of-town buyers can confirm the agent is really standing on the right plot without travelling.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to create an account to sponsor a tree?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. You can sponsor a tree as a guest with just your name, email, and phone number. You can optionally set up an account afterward to track your trees over time.

mainEntity.name: How does my certificate and tracking work?

acceptedAnswer.text: The moment your payment is confirmed, you receive a digital sponsorship certificate by email. As your tree is planted and cared for, you get its GPS map location, photo evidence, and maintenance updates — no account required to check on it.

mainEntity.name: What is the climate impact of sponsoring a tree?

acceptedAnswer.text: Each sponsored tree absorbs roughly 21 kg of CO2 per year and helps retain around 120 liters of water, adding up to measurable climate impact over time.

mainEntity.name: Are the tree planting sites approved and monitored?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Every project has full land-rights and planting approval on record, and LandCheck field agents are on the ground to plant and maintain the trees.

mainEntity.name: Can I sponsor a tree from outside Nigeria?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. LandCheck Green accepts payment in NGN or USD, so donors and diaspora anywhere in the world can sponsor a verified tree in Nigeria online.
